subject: pathology
title: Non-neoplastic leukocyte and lymph node disorders: reactive changes and key differentials

steps.tx: Leukocytosis means a raised total white cell count, usually from infection or inflammation. **Neutrophilia** is the commonest pattern in bacterial infection. When neutrophils reach 30,000 to 50,000 per microlitre or more, the picture can mimic leukaemia; this is called a **leukemoid reaction**. The cells are mature, unlike the immature myeloid cells of chronic myeloid leukaemia.

steps.tx: **Eosinophilia** is driven by IL-5 and is typically seen in allergic disease such as asthma, hay fever and drug reactions, and in **parasitic infection** such as helminths and filariasis. It also occurs in Hodgkin disease, HIV and HTLV-1. Corticosteroids cause eosinopenia instead. Eosinophil major basic protein is toxic to helminths.

steps.tx: **Infectious mononucleosis** is caused by **Epstein-Barr virus (HHV-4)**, which enters B cells via CD21. It presents with the triad of fever, pharyngitis and lymphadenopathy after an incubation of 2 to 5 weeks. The blood shows atypical lymphocytes, mostly CD8+ T cells, with Downey cells. The **monospot test** (horse erythrocyte agglutination) is the most sensitive screen; the Paul-Bunnell test uses sheep cells.
steps.say: Infectious mononucleosis is caused by Epstein-Barr virus, which enters B cells via CD21. It presents with the triad of fever, pharyngitis and lymphadenopathy after an incubation of two to five weeks. The blood shows atypical lymphocytes, mostly CD8 positive T cells, with Downey cells. The monospot test, using horse erythrocyte agglutination, is the most sensitive screen; the Paul-Bunnell test uses sheep cells.

steps.tx: Reactive **lymphadenitis** enlarges nodes draining an infected site. Histology shows cortical follicles, macrophages and many plasma cells, reflecting antigen-driven B cell activation. **Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease** (histiocytic necrotising lymphadenitis) is a benign, self-limiting condition in young women with tender cervical nodes, fever, and leukopenia in some cases. Its key feature is necrosis with karyorrhexis on excisional biopsy.
